notes.1865: Sailing junks and steamers share the Huangpu. Trading houses face a riverbank of wooden jetties and unpaved roads.
notes.1870: The waterfront grows around river trade, with merchant houses on the Bund and low fields and storehouses across the water.
notes.1875: Stone embankments and new gas lamps begin to define the promenade. Sailing vessels still crowd the river.
notes.1880: Gas lamps line the stone embankment, while steamships join the junks at Shanghai's working waterfront.
notes.1885: Trading houses and consulates give the Bund a more settled form. Docks and farmland occupy the opposite bank.
notes.1890: Rickshaws and carriages pass the Bund's merchant houses. Across the river, wharves and workshops spread along Pudong.
notes.1895: Steamship traffic gathers at the wharves as banks and trading houses expand along the waterfront.
notes.1900: Stone banks and electric streetlights mark the turn of the century. Shipyards and warehouses line the far shore.
notes.1905: Larger banks and shipping offices reshape the Bund, while Pudong remains a low waterfront of sheds and shipyards.
notes.1910: Trams and motorcars join the waterfront traffic in the final years of the Qing dynasty.
notes.1915: In the early Republic, the Bund remains a meeting place for shipping and finance. Industrial chimneys rise across the river.
notes.1918: Steamers, trams, and busy wharves animate the waterfront as the First World War draws to a close.
notes.1922: Scaffolding rises among older merchant houses, opening a new phase in the Bund's monumental architecture.
notes.1925: Crowds and political unrest mark the waterfront, as taller buildings begin to replace the older trading houses.
notes.1928: The HSBC dome and Customs House clock tower anchor a new skyline, with Sassoon House still taking shape.
notes.1930: Sassoon House joins the Customs House and HSBC Building, giving the Bund its familiar outline of stone, domes, and towers.
notes.1932: The Bund's grand facades stand above a tense riverfront in the aftermath of fighting in Shanghai.
notes.1935: A new Bank of China building rises beside Sassoon House, adding another layer to the Bund's stone skyline.
notes.1937: Warships gather on the Huangpu. The Bund's established skyline overlooks a city entering war.
notes.1941: Warships and checkpoints interrupt daily life along the Bund, while industry continues across the river.
notes.1943: Under Japanese occupation, patrol boats and military notices mark a waterfront shaped by wartime control.
notes.1946: River traffic returns to a waterfront still bearing the marks of war, with repaired facades and damaged docks.
notes.1950: New flags appear on the Bund's older buildings as Shanghai enters the early years of the People's Republic.
notes.1955: Bicycles and buses pass the stone facades. Barges work the river beside Pudong's warehouses and docks.
notes.1960: Tugs and barges move through the industrial haze, beneath a skyline still defined by the Bund's older buildings.
notes.1965: The Bund's stone buildings overlook a working river of barges and tugs, with low factories along the opposite bank.
notes.1970: Political banners reshape the appearance of the Bund during the Cultural Revolution. Pudong remains an industrial shoreline.
notes.1975: Bicycles crowd the waterfront beneath political billboards, while warehouses and cranes line the far bank.
notes.1978: The first signs of reform appear along the promenade. Across the Huangpu, Pudong remains a landscape of docks and warehouses.
notes.1982: Commercial signs and visitors return to the Bund, while ferries connect it to Pudong's low waterfront.
notes.1985: Tourists and new advertising bring color to the promenade. Ferries still cross to a shore of docks and housing.
notes.1988: The Bund grows busier with visitors and traffic, while Pudong's low roofline gives little hint of the towers to come.
notes.1990: Cleared ground and piling rigs mark the beginning of Pudong's redevelopment, among the warehouses of the old riverfront.
notes.1992: The Oriental Pearl Tower rises from a construction site on the far bank, its concrete structure surrounded by cranes.
notes.1993: The Oriental Pearl's pink spheres take their place above Pudong, while work continues on its slender spire.
notes.1994: The Oriental Pearl gives the river a new landmark, rising above the construction sites of a changing Pudong.
notes.1995: The completed Oriental Pearl stands above the low riverfront, the first prominent marker of Lujiazui's new skyline.
notes.1997: The Oriental Pearl overlooks a district of cranes and rising towers, as Lujiazui begins to fill the eastern horizon.
notes.1998: Jin Mao's tiered crown nears completion above Lujiazui, where cranes mark a skyline still taking shape.
notes.2000: The completed Jin Mao Tower joins the Oriental Pearl, while new office towers begin to fill the space around them.
notes.2002: Jin Mao and the Oriental Pearl stand above a growing cluster of towers on the eastern bank of the Huangpu.
notes.2004: Glass towers gather around Jin Mao and the Oriental Pearl, giving Lujiazui a denser urban silhouette.
notes.2006: The Shanghai World Financial Center rises above its neighbors, with cranes still working at its unfinished crown.
notes.2008: The completed Shanghai World Financial Center adds its distinctive open crown to the skyline beside Jin Mao.
notes.2010: In the year of Shanghai's World Expo, Lujiazui's towers face the Bund across a river busy with excursion boats.
notes.2012: Three landmarks define the skyline: the Oriental Pearl, Jin Mao, and the open crown of the World Financial Center.
notes.2013: Shanghai Tower reaches its full height, its twisting form still crowned by cranes and exposed steelwork.
notes.2014: Work continues at Shanghai Tower's crown, as its curved glass facade rises above the neighboring towers.
notes.2015: Shanghai Tower's completed glass exterior brings a new height and a turning profile to Lujiazui.
notes.2017: The completed Shanghai Tower joins the Oriental Pearl, Jin Mao, and the World Financial Center above a dense riverfront.
notes.2018: A dense skyline of glass towers now faces the Bund, with sightseeing boats passing along the Huangpu.
notes.2020: The towers of Lujiazui face the Bund across the Huangpu, tracing the transformation of a once low industrial shore.
